articles.title: Gold Shines Despite High Rates... Gold ETFs Rally
articles.description: Gold prices are regaining momentum after a period of consolidation, lifting returns on gold-related exchange-traded funds (ETFs). While higher interest rates typically reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold, mounting concerns over U.S. fiscal conditions and increased Treasury supply are instead fueling demand for the precious metal as a safe haven. Jewelry is displayed at a gold shop in Seoul. /News1 According to the financial investment industry on Aug. 23, December gold futures on the COMEX division of the New York Mercantile Exchange closed at $4,571.40 per ounce on Aug. 20, up $26.10, or 0.6%, from the previous session. The settlement marked the highest level since late May. December gold futures have climbed about 13% in just over a month after falling to $4,048.70 per ounce on July 16. The rally is particularly notable because gold has continued to strengthen even as long-term U.S. interest rates have surged. The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury briefly climbed to 5.31% on Aug. 17, its highest level since 2007. Gold prices and interest rates generally tend to move in opposite directions. Because gold does not pay interest, rising rates typically increase the relative attractiveness of yield-bearing assets such as bonds. Recently, however, the factors driving long-term yields higher — concerns over the U.S. fiscal burden and growing Treasury issuance — have reinforced gold's appeal as both an alternative to dollar-denominated assets and a safe haven. “This year, oil prices surged following the U.S.-Iran war, heightening inflation concerns and pushing interest rates higher, while gold prices underwent a correction for about five months,” said Ko Kyung-bum, an analyst at Yuanta Securities. “More recently, despite rising interest rates stemming from fiscal concerns, the dollar has weakened amid joint intervention by the United States and Japan and easing concerns over further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve following a slowdown in employment,” Ko said. “That has helped gold regain strength.” The rise in gold prices has also boosted the performance of gold-related ETFs. NH-Amundi Asset Management's HANARO Global Gold Mining Companies ETF posted a one-month return of 30.46%, the highest among gold-related ETFs listed in Korea. The gain far exceeded the roughly 11% increase in international gold prices over the same period. Unlike ETFs that invest directly in gold futures or physical bullion, the fund invests in global gold miners including Newmont, Agnico Eagle Mines and Barrick Mining. When gold prices rise, mining companies can see their revenue and earnings increase at a faster pace than the underlying metal, allowing their shares to outperform during a gold rally. The same operating leverage, however, can magnify losses when gold prices decline. “Investing in gold mining companies can provide exposure to rising gold prices while also offering the potential for excess returns through a leverage effect, creating an opportunity to enhance portfolio returns,” said Kim Seung-chul, head of ETF Investment at NH-Amundi Asset Management. “Investors should also keep in mind that because the fund invests in mining stocks rather than gold itself, the leverage effect can work in the opposite direction when gold prices fall,” Kim added. Other gold-related ETFs have also delivered strong returns. Korea Investment Management's ACE Gold Futures Leverage ETF gained 23.52% over the past month, while Mirae Asset Global Investments' TIGER Gold Futures (H) ETF rose 11.55% and Samsung Asset Management's KODEX Gold Futures ETF advanced 11.27%. ETFs investing in physical gold also posted gains, with ACE KRX Physical Gold and TIGER KRX Physical Gold rising 5.99% and 5.44%, respectively, over the past month. Retail investors are also returning to the gold market. According to the Korea Exchange, individual investors made net purchases of about 149.1 billion won ($100 million) in the KRX gold market between Aug. 1 and Aug. 20. The buying marked a reversal from the previous three months, when retail investors were net sellers of gold from May through July. Institutional demand is also emerging. The Bank of Korea disclosed through a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Aug. 12 that it held 679,765 shares of SPDR Gold Shares, a U.S.-listed gold ETF. The position was valued at about $250.41 million, or roughly 355 billion won, at the end of the second quarter. It marked the Bank of Korea's first investment in a gold-related financial product since its purchase of physical gold in 2013. Market observers expect gold prices to retain upward momentum for the time being. Although the U.S. Treasury has expanded the scale of its buybacks of longer-dated government bonds, fundamental factors putting upward pressure on long-term yields — including the U.S. fiscal deficit and heavy Treasury issuance — remain unresolved. Persistent concerns over fiscal sustainability could weaken confidence in the dollar and sustain demand for gold as a hedge. “The U.S. Treasury has doubled the size of its long-term bond buybacks, but there are limits to how much this can address the fundamental drivers behind rising long-term interest rates,” Ko said. “With concerns over fiscal soundness persisting, declining confidence in the dollar is likely to remain a factor supporting the upward trend in gold prices,” he added. Still, several factors could limit further gains. An escalation in geopolitical uncertainty, particularly in the Middle East, could weaken appetite for risk assets and increase volatility across financial markets. Gold could also experience greater short-term swings depending on movements in long-term interest rates and the U.S. dollar. “If the situation involving Iran remains unresolved through September and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continue, expectations of Fed tightening could intensify, putting downward pressure on gold prices,” said Hong Sung-ki, an analyst at LS Securities. viayou@chosunbiz.com

articles.title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7219 – Reuters estimate
articles.description: The People’s Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day’s closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point. A stronger-than-expected CNY midpoint is typically read as a sign the PBOC is leaning against depreciation pressure, while a weaker fixing for the CNY can indicate tolerance for a softer currency, often in response to dollar strength or domestic economic headwinds.In periods of heightened global volatility, such as shifts in US rate expectations, trade tensions or capital flow pressures, the fixing takes on added significance. For investors, it provides insight into Beijing’s currency priorities, balancing competitiveness, capital stability and financial market confidence. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Shein’s stock listing is almost here: Why the fast fashion giant has a much smaller valuation for its upcoming IPO
articles.description: Shein Global Holdings, the fast fashion giant, is planning to make its long-awaited stock market debut in Hong Kong next month. Known for producing and selling inexpensive clothing and apparel, Shein was founded in 2008 in China, but is now headquartered in Singapore. The company has been a big hit with younger consumers and saw its sales and user growth soar during the pandemic-era lockdowns. Its valuation reportedly topped out at around $100 billion in 2022. However, weaker sales, higher costs, and geopolitical tensions have taken their toll, and with its market debut, Shein is now targeting a valuation of closer to $27 billion, a filing on Monday reveals—a nearly 75% decline over four years. The company has flirted with IPOs in both London and New York in recent years , but scuttled those plans for several reasons, including challenges by U.S. lawmakers. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while serving as a senator, led the charge to urge U.S. regulators to stop Shein’s IPO process in early 2024, arguing that its reporting would not be transparent. Almost three years later, Shein appears primed to finally go public, albeit with a considerably downsized valuation. Why did Shein’s valuation fall? Last month, Shein reported a quarterly loss due to slowing sales and fallout from a change to import duty exemptions on small packages brought on by President Trump. The change did away with the “de minimis exemption” that had allowed goods valued at less than $800 to avoid tariffs. Accordingly, during the first quarter of 2026, Shein lost $99 million on $9.05 billion in revenue. That was down from net income of $395 million on $8.95 billion in revenue a year earlier, according to Shein’s prospectus. Shein’s filing warns that it could continue to see adverse effects on its business due to tariffs, the war in Iran, and more. “We have grown rapidly since our inception, and there is no assurance that our growth will continue,” the filing reads. Even so, for investors who have been waiting to snap up shares of a company with 281 million active users, the long-awaited opportunity is finally approaching. Shein is expected to list its shares on Tuesday, September 1.
